resources.name: Open-source periodic DFT code (e.g., Quantum ESPRESSO, CP2K, ABINIT)

access.notes: Any DFT code supporting structural relaxation, symmetry-constrained optimization, frozen-phonon calculations, and Born effective charge computation.

resources.notes: Replaces the proprietary CRYSTAL code used in the original paper.

resources.name: Pseudopotentials and basis sets for Bi, Ti, O

access.notes: Bi: ECP78MWB quasirelativistic pseudopotential + 4s3p1d/2s2p1d basis. Ti: Hay-Wadt small-core pseudopotential + 6s6p5d/3s3p3d basis. O: all-electron 14s6p/4s3p basis augmented with a d exponent of 0.5. Available from cited literature (Refs. 26,27,28 in the paper). Equivalent pseudopotentials from standard public libraries (e.g., SSSP, PseudoDojo) may be substituted.

resources.notes: Specific norm-conserving pseudopotentials used in the original study; the agent may use suitable alternatives that produce comparable accuracy.

resources.name: Ideal Fd-3m pyrochlore structure for Bi2Ti2O6O'

access.notes: Standard cubic pyrochlore: space group Fd-3m (origin choice 2), Bi at (0.5,0.5,0.5), Ti at (0,0,0), O at (0.375,0.375,0.375), O' at (x,0.125,0.125) with initial x ≈ 0.3125 or literature value 0.325. Lattice constant a = 10.376 Å. The agent can construct this from published coordinates.

resources.notes: Widely known crystal structure; the agent builds the starting cell from these coordinates.

resources.name: Symmetry analysis tool (e.g., spglib, findsym)

access.notes: Used to detect the Pna2_1 space group from the relaxed P1 coordinates and to generate the 44-atom primitive cell.
